memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "It is a day of sabbath rest, and you must deny yourselves; it is a lasting ordinance. The priest who is anointed and ordained to succeed his father as high priest is to make atonement. He is to put on the sacred linen garments and make atonement for the Most Holy Place, for the tent of meeting and the altar, and for the priests and all the members of the community." - Lev 16:31-33 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Look at the phrase tucked into verse 32: the priest who is anointed and ordained to succeed his father.

Aaron would die. Another would take his place, and then another, and another. The Day of Atonement would come around every year, and each time a new man in the same linen garments would walk behind the same curtain with the same blood.

Hebrews puts its finger on exactly this weakness. Now there have been many of those priests, since death prevented them from continuing in office; but because Jesus lives for ever, he has a permanent priesthood (Heb 7:23-24).

A permanent priesthood. No successor needed. No handover. No year in which the office stood vacant.

And then the conclusion: therefore he is able to save completely those who come to God through him, because he always lives to intercede for them (Heb 7:25).

Right now, as you read this, Jesus is interceding for you. Not remembering you occasionally. Continuously. He does not tire, retire, or die.

Every high priest of Israel eventually failed His people by dying. Yours never will.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What does it mean to you that Christ is interceding right now?
2. How does a permanent priesthood give you more security than a temporary one?
3. Where do you need to trust that He is able to save you "completely"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You that You are a Priest for ever who never dies and never hands over. Thank You that You are praying for me right now. I trust You to save me completely. Amen.
